title: Saving Radio City Music Hall: An Author Talk with Rosemary Novellino-Mearns
description: Unbelievable as it sounds, in 1978, Radio City Music Hall — an Art Deco masterpiece and one of New York City’s iconic tourist attractions and cultural landmarks — was slated for demolition.Rosemary Novellino-Mearns, Dance Captain of the Radio City Music Hall Ballet Company during the 1970s, recounts the remarkable true story of how she rallied colleagues, friends, members of the media, and political allies to challenge the Rockefeller establishment and, against all odds, save "The Showplace of the Nation."Join Rosemary at the BHS Castle for this special presentation. A Q&A and book signing will follow.Cost is $10 for BHS members and $15 for non-members.Purchase tickets at baysidehistorical.org/events-1/saving-radio-city-music-hall-an-author-talk-with-rosemary-novellino-mearns.This event is part of the Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.
location: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)

title: Friends of Starlight Park Meeting
description: Join Friends of Starlight park in their monthly team meetings!The mission of Friends of Starlight Park is to bring surrounding communities together by caring for the park, promoting safety, and encouraging its use as a shared resource for recreation and community events. title: Volunteer Day: Clara's Garden
description: GreenThumb community gardens are developed, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces.Clara's Garden is a quiet green oasis in East New York that is seeking volunteers to help us finish our garden makeover! Join us for a hands-on volunteer day to place beds, mulch, and prepare the garden for winter! No prior experience necessary - beginners are welcome! Come learn about the community gardens in the neighborhood. GreenThumb will provide supplies and facilitation.This is a great opportunity to support a dynamic community space while learning about urban agriculture. Please wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks. Note: Some tasks may involve lifting heavy materials and extended periods of bending, squatting, and moving.Register here! Location: 579 Glenmore Ave, Brooklyn, NY 11207For information about group volunteering, please contact Volunteer Program Coordinator, Olivia Navarro at Olivia.Navarro@parks.nyc.govThis event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

title: Proximity Exhibition
description: Featuring work by: Erin Butler, Linda Butti, Mary Campbell, Lisa Dahl, Griselda Healy, Craig Manister, Ann Marie McDonnell, Mike Shane, Gayle Tanaka, Martha Trivizas. Celebrating Snug Harbor’s longstanding studio program, where artists in residence create new work within its historic buildings, PROXIMITY explores the studio as a generative space: artists working near one another across space, time, and relationship. Spanning painting, photography, and mixed media, PROXIMITY is not defined by a shared aesthetic, but by a condition of closeness. Here, proximity becomes more than a matter of place—it becomes a context through which individual practices develop, intersect, and inform one another.  When: October 2 - December 13Fridays & Saturdays, 12:00 PM-7:00 PM | Sundays, 11:00 AM- 5:00 PMWhere: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Main Hall Gallery, Building C  (View Site Map and Directions)Admission:$5.00 – General Admission$4.00 – Students/SeniorsPlease note: On October 16, we will host an opening reception for PROXIMITY from 6-8 PM. Visiting during those hours will be free. Please RSVP to the reception here: https://snug-harbor.org/event/proximity-opening-reception/ PROXIMITY is made possible through generous support from the New York State Council on the Arts with the support of Governor Kathy Hochul and the New York State Legislature, the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs in partnership with the City Council, and the Samuel I. Newhouse Foundation.
location: Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art (Building C) (in Snug Harbor Cultural Center)

title: Workshop for Volunteers–Let’s Get Outside: Engaging Youth in Park Stewardship
description: Is your grassroots organization wondering how to better involve children and teens in your park or greenspace? Join us for an interactive workshop covering the basics of engaging kids in environmental stewardship, including best practices and smart tips. We’ll discuss how to customize your engagement to different age groups, from kindergarteners to young adults. Dinner will be provided, and we’ll close the event with a stewardship kit giveaway! Registration for this session is required and will close the day before the event. At Partnerships for Parks, we help people, organizations, and government work together to support parks, gardens, trees, and other green and open spaces in New York City. Our free workshops are a great way to network and learn the skills needed to start, build, or sustain a community group dedicated to local parks.
